active_paradigms.idea: Massively expand the multi-start portfolio with many deterministic jitter seeds and adaptive time budgeting
active_paradigms.description: The current program only evaluates 4 candidates. Since the objective function _gpu_load_objective is cheap and vectorized, generate 50-200 candidates by varying the multiplicative jitter pattern (different eps values like 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2 and different modular patterns e.g. % 11, % 13, prime-based hashes) across both hierarchical and global policies, plus variations of the swap-refinement iteration count (4, 8, 16, 32). Score each with the evaluator-aligned objective and keep the best. Use a wall-clock budget check (time.monotonic against a self-imposed limit like 200s) to stop generating candidates so runtime never blows the evaluator timeout. Because candidates differ only in tie-breaking, this directly reduces max per-(layer,gpu) load without changing algorithm structure.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: load-balance quality (max per-GPU load) while keeping algorithm runtime bounded
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep everything in vectorized torch CPU ops with num_threads=1 (evaluator forces single thread); measure objective cost per candidate and cap candidate count accordingly; ensure jitter never reorders weights enough to change hierarchical group packing semantics drastically (keep eps small).

active_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy max-load replication with water-filling / proportional replication counts decided jointly with placement
active_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts greedily replicates the expert with highest weight/logcnt, one replica at a time, which is myopic. Instead, compute replication counts analytically: solve for counts c_i >= 1, sum(c_i) = num_phy that minimize sum over experts of ceil-like imbalance — e.g., water-filling where each expert's effective load weight_i/c_i is driven toward the common target T = total_tokens / num_phy, choosing c_i = max(1, round(weight_i / T)) then fixing the sum by incrementing/decrementing the experts with largest residual weight_i/c_i. Then place replicas with the existing balanced_packing. This decouples the (currently coupled) replication and placement decisions in a principled way and is O(num_log) per layer, fully vectorized.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: balance quality: reduces the max effective per-replica load that placement must then equalize; also faster than the num_redundant sequential loop
active_paradigms.cautions: Must guarantee all counts >= 1 and sum exactly num_phy - num_log extra; validate the resulting logcnt tensor is consistent with phy2log and rank tensors exactly as the evaluator checks; keep the greedy version as a portfolio fallback candidate since it may win on some workloads.

active_paradigms.idea: Direct min-max local search on the final GPU assignment: replica moves and swaps across GPUs optimizing the true objective
active_paradigms.description: After producing the best portfolio candidate, run a refinement pass that operates directly on physical-to-GPU placement: identify the (layer, gpu) with maximum load and the (layer, gpu) with minimum load, and move or swap one physical expert between them whenever it strictly reduces max load (or the sum-of-squares tiebreaker without increasing max). Unlike the existing intra-packing swap (which is constrained to heaviest/lightest pack pairs and equal-count packs), this operates on the final solution with full freedom, including moving a replica to an underloaded GPU even if counts become unequal (per-GPU expert counts need not be exactly equal unless the evaluator enforces it — check and if enforced, use swaps only). Iterate until no improving move exists, vectorized across layers. This is a different failure mode from the earlier numpy local search because it uses the exact evaluator objective, torch vectorization across all layers simultaneously, and starts from an already-strong solution.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: the exact evaluator objective (max per-(layer,gpu) load plus sum-of-squares tiebreaker) — closing the gap between heuristic packing and the true metric
active_paradigms.cautions: Verify whether the evaluator requires exactly num_replicas/num_gpus experts per GPU; if so restrict to swaps. Keep move evaluation vectorized (compute per-GPU loads once, evaluate all candidate moves as tensor ops) to stay within the runtime budget; cap iterations (e.g., 50 passes) with early exit when max-load stops improving.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy LPT packing with Karmarkar-Karp differencing plus a min-max local search on GPU loads
tried_paradigms.description: The current balanced_packing uses greedy assignment then a narrow heaviest<->lightest swap loop. Instead, formulate the final GPU packing step as an explicit makespan minimization: first run the existing LPT to get an initial feasible solution, then run a vectorized local search that considers ALL (source GPU, dest GPU, expert) move/swap pairs per layer, accepting any move that strictly reduces max load (or sum of squares above the mean). Iterate until no improving move exists or a time budget (~2-3 seconds) is exhausted. This directly targets the max-GPU-load metric, which dominates the balance score, while keeping the vectorized numpy implementation fast enough for the runtime component of the score.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary balance score (max GPU load / mean load) with bounded runtime
tried_paradigms.cautions: Vectorize over layers with numpy; cap iterations by wall-clock time; ensure each pack still holds exactly num_phy/num_gpus experts; keep deterministic tie-breaking for reproducibility.
tried_paradigms.approach_type: numpy local search (custom vectorized min-max refinement)

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment for replica-to-GPU placement with cost matrix penalizing load imbalance
tried_paradigms.description: After replication counts are decided, the assignment of physical experts to GPUs is a structured assignment problem. Build a cost matrix per layer where entry (expert, gpu) encodes the resulting GPU load if this expert were placed there (e.g., current tentative load of gpu + expert weight), then solve a rectangular assignment (each expert to one slot, each slot capacity respected by expanding gpu columns into slot columns) with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Repeat 3-5 rounds: each round recompute costs from the current loads and re-solve; this converges quickly to near-optimal min-max placements and replaces the heuristic packing entirely. Slots enforce the exact per-GPU expert-count constraint naturally via the expanded cost matrix.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Balance metric via globally optimal per-round assignment; runtime stays low since the assignment problem is solved exactly and quickly.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Expand GPUs into (gpu, slot) columns so cardinality constraints hold; handle the rectangular case (experts <= slots) that linear_sum_assignment supports; batch layers by solving each layer independently; use float64 costs scaled to avoid numerical issues.

tried_paradigms.idea: Binary-search the target max load and decide replication counts jointly with load, using a feasibility greedy
tried_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts greedily replicates the highest load/copy expert, which is suboptimal because replication counts and placement interact. Instead, binary search a target per-GPU load T (between mean load and max load). For each T, decide replication counts so that ceil(w_i / T) replicas are allocated to each expert (capped by total physical budget, redistributing leftover replicas to the largest w_i/ceil(w_i/T) ratios), then check if all experts fit on GPUs under T using LPT with capacity T. This directly minimizes the theoretical lower bound on max load and produces replica counts matched to the achievable placement rather than chosen blindly. Use ~20 binary search iterations on a scalar, which is very fast.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Both the max-load lower bound (via optimal replication counts) and runtime (scalar binary search, vectorized feasibility check).
tried_paradigms.cautions: Handle the case where minimum total replicas (sum of ceil(w_i/T)) exceeds the physical budget: raise T accordingly; keep counts >= 1; ensure num_replicas total exactly; fall back to current greedy if the search fails.
tried_paradigms.approach_type: bisection on target load with capacity-driven replication (numpy)

tried_paradigms.idea: Optimal replication counts via water-filling binary search instead of greedy replicate_experts
tried_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts greedily picks the expert with max weight/logcnt, which is suboptimal. Instead, for each layer solve for replication counts directly: given R redundant experts, find integer counts c_i >= 1 with sum c_i = num_phy that minimizes max_i(w_i/c_i). This is solvable near-optimally: binary search on the target max load T, and for each T compute needed count ceil(w_i/T) per expert; find the smallest feasible T where sum ceil(w_i/T) <= num_phy, then distribute leftover replicas to experts with largest resulting w_i/c_i. This is a classic water-filling solution and is vectorized across all layers simultaneously with torch tensor ops (each binary search step is one tensor op over the whole batch). It typically achieves 5-15% lower max load than greedy and is O(log(max_w) * num_layers * num_log) — faster than the current O(num_redundant) sequential loop.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary load-balance score (min-max replica load) and algorithm runtime (replaces sequential replication loop with ~40 vectorized binary-search steps)
tried_paradigms.cautions: After binary search, some experts may have count > 1 but leftover replicas must be assigned carefully: assign remaining replicas one at a time (or via a vectorized argmax of w_i/c_i) to keep feasibility. Ensure counts sum exactly to num_phy and every logical expert has at least 1 replica. Keep per-node decomposition from the hierarchical scheme.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace greedy LPT + limited swap refinement with Hungarian-style assignment refinement using scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment
tried_paradigms.description: The balanced_packing greedy LPT followed by 16 heaviest/lightest swap iterations is a weak local search that only considers one pair of packs at a time. A stronger refinement: after greedy initialization, run repeated pairwise rebalancing where for the two most-loaded and least-loaded packs, solve the optimal reassignment of their combined 2*groups_per_pack items between the two packs exactly (this is a balanced partition problem solvable by sorting / subset selection), guaranteeing each pair is optimally split. Even better: for the final GPU packing step (Step 3), where each GPU gets exactly phy_experts_per_gpu items, formulate the refinement as a linear assignment problem: pick a candidate set of items and slots and use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on a cost matrix designed to equalize loads (cost = |item_weight - target_slot_load|), iterating a few rounds. Since the evaluator runs single-threaded with torch threads=1, scipy on CPU is competitive and linear_sum_assignment is exact for each subproblem.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Load-balance quality (lower max and variance of pack loads at both node-packing and GPU-packing stages)
tried_paradigms.cautions: scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment cost is O(n^3); keep the assignment subproblems small (only refine the top-k and bottom-k packs, e.g., k=4, or pairwise between extreme packs). Batch layers: process each layer's refinement independently but reuse the same code; the workload likely has modest layer counts so this stays within the 360s timeout. Must preserve the exact cardinality constraint (each pack keeps exactly groups_per_pack items) — use square cost matrices of size 2*groups_per_pack for pairwise refinement.

tried_paradigms.idea: Global (non-hierarchical) rebalancing with multi-start perturbation and best-of-N selection
tried_paradigms.description: The current algorithm always uses the hierarchical policy when num_groups % num_nodes == 0, forcing groups to stay node-local, which can be far from globally optimal when load is skewed across groups. Add a global policy path: treat all logical experts uniformly, compute replication counts via water-filling globally, then pack all physical experts to GPUs with balanced_packing, and compare the resulting objective (e.g., max per-GPU load or sum of squared loads) against the hierarchical result, returning whichever is better. Additionally, add a cheap multi-start: run the packing with a few deterministic perturbations of the sort order (e.g., rotate starting pack offsets, or jitter tie-breaking) and keep the best result by the evaluator-aligned objective computed locally. This is a portfolio approach: since scoring is deterministic, evaluating the true objective inside rebalance_experts and keeping the best of a handful of runs directly improves the score with only linear time cost.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score via escaping the hierarchical policy's structural constraint; robustness across workload scenarios
tried_paradigms.cautions: Must compute the local objective identically to the evaluator's notion of balance (check evaluator.py's metric — likely max GPU load or variance of per-GPU token counts including replica-count division). Keep total runtime bounded: 3-5 starts maximum, each fully vectorized. Ensure the global path still respects num_gpus divisibility and produces valid logical_to_physical_map with rank indices filling maxlogcnt slots correctly (scatter-based construction already handles this).
